# Temple Scroll Column 2 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 2 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 2:2 — "glory dwelling" — rendering of the Shekinah concept

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I-will-cause-to-dwell [my] glory" | Preserves hif'il causative verb form and construct |
| LOGOS | "I will cause my glory to dwell" | Standard formal rendering of the shakan hif'il |
| PNEUMA | "I will settle my glorious presence" | Dynamic rendering; "glorious presence" for kavod |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. "Glory" (kavod) must be preserved as a distinct noun, not absorbed into an adjective as PNEUMA does. EMET's hyphenation is unnecessary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:4 — "yom ha-beri'ah" — "day of creation"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-day-of-creation" | Hyphenated construct chain |
| LOGOS | "the day of creation" | Literal rendering of the phrase |
| PNEUMA | "the day of new creation" | Adds "new" to clarify the eschatological sense |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "the day of creation." PNEUMA's addition of "new" is interpretive — the Hebrew does not contain any word for "new." The eschatological sense is clear from context without adding words.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:4 — "I shall create my temple" — verb choice for bara'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I-shall-create my-temple" | bara' rendered "create" — the theologically loaded term |
| LOGOS | "I shall create my temple" | Same verb choice, standard syntax |
| PNEUMA | "I will build my temple" | "Build" for clarity; the temple is being constructed |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET rendering "create." The use of bara' (create) rather than banah (build) is theologically significant — God creates the eschatological temple by divine fiat, not human construction. PNEUMA's "build" obscures this distinction.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 2:9 — "berit 'olam" — eternal covenant phrasing

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-covenant of-eternity" | Construct chain preserved |
| LOGOS | "an everlasting covenant" | Standard biblical English phrasing |
| PNEUMA | "a covenant that will last forever" | Expanded paraphrase for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "an everlasting covenant." This is the standard biblical English phrase (cf. Gen 17:7, Isa 55:3). PNEUMA's expansion is unnecessary; EMET's construct is overly wooden.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:12 — "sanctuary" vs. "holy place"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "my-sanctuary for-ever-and-ever" | miqdash as "sanctuary" with doubled temporal phrase |
| LOGOS | "my sanctuary forever" | Standard rendering |
| PNEUMA | "my holy place forever" | Dynamic equivalent of miqdash |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "my sanctuary forever." "Sanctuary" (miqdash) is the established English term. PNEUMA's "holy place" is too generic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements: 5*
*Resolution: LOGOS 3, LOGOS/EMET 1, EMET 0, PNEUMA 0, Compromise 0*
